root_cause.text: In `drivers/power/supply/ab8500_charger.c`, the driver used `devm_request_threaded_irq()` before registering the `power_supply` object, so `devm` teardown freed/unregistered the `power_supply` before the IRQ handler was removed, allowing an interrupt to call `power_supply_changed()` on a freed or uninitialized `power_supply` during probe/remove races.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the entire “Request interrupts” block from before `di->usb_chg.psy` registration to after it, and the CVE text explicitly says the bug was caused by “requesting IRQ before the `devm_` variant for allocating/registering the `power_supply` handle,” which led to a race where the IRQ handler used a freed/uninitialized handle in `power_supply_changed()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove charger IRQ registration from probe so the driver no longer depends on those interrupts during initialization.
intent_record.what: The probe function `ab8500_charger_probe()` had an entire block removed that iterated over `ab8500_charger_irq`, looked up each IRQ by name with `platform_get_irq_byname()`, and registered threaded interrupt handlers via `devm_request_threaded_irq()` with logging on failure/success.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the driver no longer requests or installs those charger-related IRQ handlers during probe, so interrupt-driven charger event handling from this code path is disabled or deferred elsewhere; this also eliminates the possibility of probe failure from missing IRQs or IRQ request errors in this block.

intent_record.intent_summary: Register the charger driver's required IRQs during probe and fail if any interrupt cannot be acquired.
intent_record.what: In ab8500_charger_probe(), a new block was added after registering the USB power supply that iterates over ab8500_charger_irq, looks up each IRQ by name with platform_get_irq_byname(), and registers a threaded interrupt handler for each one using devm_request_threaded_irq() with IRQF_SHARED | IRQF_NO_SUSPEND | IRQF_ONESHOT. It also adds error logging and returns on failure, plus a debug log on success.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the charger driver now actively acquires and handles its named interrupts during probe instead of leaving them unregistered. This enables charger-related interrupt events to be serviced, and causes probe to fail early if any required IRQ is missing or cannot be requested, preventing the driver from running without its needed interrupt handling.

Register the charger driver's required IRQs during probe and fail if any interrupt cannot be acquired.

relevance_review.reason: The change removes IRQ registration from probe, which directly addresses the race where an IRQ could fire before the power_supply is safely registered or after teardown begins. This matches the root cause involving devm-managed IRQ/power_supply ordering in ab8500_charger.c.
The change concerns IRQ registration order during probe, which is directly tied to the race where an IRQ handler could run before the power_supply is safely registered or after it is torn down.

candidates.rationale: Requesting charger IRQs with devm-managed teardown during probe is the direct cause of the race: the IRQ can still fire while the power_supply object is not yet registered or is being torn down, leading to power_supply_changed() being called on an invalid object.
This loop performs the early IRQ acquisition during probe; the vulnerability stems from doing this before the power_supply lifecycle is safely established.
This line is part of the premature interrupt setup path that enables the race window by obtaining and then requesting charger interrupts during initialization.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the direct premature IRQ registration site. Using devm-managed IRQ setup during probe allowed charger interrupts to remain active while the power_supply object was not yet safely registered or was being torn down, enabling the race where the handler could call power_supply_changed() on an invalid object.

This loop is the probe-time IRQ acquisition path that established the unsafe ordering. It iterates over charger interrupts during initialization before the power_supply lifecycle is fully established, creating the window for the teardown race.

This statement is part of the early interrupt setup that feeds the later devm_request_threaded_irq() registration. It contributes to the vulnerable ordering by obtaining charger IRQs during probe, before the power_supply object is safely in place.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 1c1f13a006ed0d71bb5664c8b7e3e77a28da3beb
Author: Linus Walleij <linusw@kernel.org>
Date:   Sun May 23 00:50:39 2021 +0200

    power: supply: ab8500: Move to componentized binding
    
    The driver has problems with the different components of
    the charging code racing with each other to probe().
    
    This results in all four subdrivers populating battery
    information to ascertain that it is populated for their
    own needs for example.
    
    Fix this by using component pr
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is no longer present in this version. The root cause was that IRQs were requested before power-supply registration, allowing an interrupt handler to race with teardown and call into an uninitialized/freed power_supply. In this snippet, the code uses `devm_request_threaded_irq()` in probe, but the handler setup is now part of a componentized bind flow and the power supplies are registered with `devm_power_supply_register()` before the component bind completes. Specifically, the old pattern `request_threaded_irq(...); ... power_supply_register(...)` is gone. The new code shows `devm_power_supply_register(dev, &ab8500_ac_chg_desc, ...)` and `devm_power_supply_register(dev, &ab8500_usb_chg_desc, ...)`, and IRQs are requested with `devm_request_threaded_irq()` in probe before `component_master_add_with_match()`, while execution/child binding is deferred until `ab8500_charger_bind()`. The remove path also uses `component_master_del()` and no longer manually frees IRQs or unregisters power supplies, indicating the lifetime ordering issue has been addressed.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable ordering described in the root cause is no longer present in this snippet. The driver now requests IRQs early with devm_request_threaded_irq(): `ret = devm_request_threaded_irq(dev, irq, NULL, ab8500_charger_irq[i].isr, ...)`, and the power supplies are also devm-managed: `di->ac_chg.psy = devm_power_supply_register(...)` and `di->usb_chg.psy = devm_power_supply_register(...)`. More importantly, the commit moves actual execution into component binding: the comment says probes only initialize data structures and `no execution happens until the .bind() callback is called`, and the bind path creates the workqueue and calls `component_bind_all(dev, di)`. This means the IRQ handlers are no longer able to run before the componentized setup has completed, so the specific bug of an IRQ calling `power_supply_changed()` on a freed/uninitialized power_supply during probe/remove races is not present here. The removal path also uses `component_master_del(&pdev->dev, &ab8500_charger_comp_ops)` and no longer manually frees IRQs before unregistering power supplies, which is consistent with the fix.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable pattern described in the root cause is not present in this function body. The IRQs are requested early (`for (i = 0; i < ARRAY_SIZE(ab8500_charger_irq); i++) { ... ret = devm_request_threaded_irq(...); }` at lines 3452-3467), but the power_supply objects are also registered in this same probe path (`di->ac_chg.psy = devm_power_supply_register(...)` at 3574-3582 and `di->usb_chg.psy = devm_power_supply_register(...)` at 3585-3593). More importantly, this commit has been reworked into a componentized binding: after setup it calls `component_master_add_with_match(&pdev->dev, &ab8500_charger_comp_ops, match);` at 3649-3655, which changes the binding/teardown ordering away from the old unsafe probe/remove race. Since the exact old bug-inducing construct (IRQ setup before power_supply registration with no ordering fix) is not shown as a vulnerable standalone path here, and the commit clearly introduces the component framework intended to address the race, this function already contains the fix.
